scope_note: Initial discovery and gap-closure audit for the selected 315,400-square-foot IM3 building footprint at Meta's Altoona campus in Polk County. Public records generally describe the multi-building Siculus/Meta campus, state incentive contracts, later ATN phases, or company-county accounts rather than the selected building; every quantitative observation therefore remains unallocated and no campus amount is area-apportioned to the selected footprint.

sources.title: A New Data Center for Iowa
sources.notes: Facebook announced its fourth owned-and-operated data center in Altoona, expected construction to begin in summer 2013, and expected service in 2014. The release documents original-project chronology but gives no building identifier, realized investment, payroll, supplier spending, tax payment, utility use, or public cost.

sources.title: Facebook's Altoona Data Center is Now Online
sources.notes: Operator announcement establishes that the Altoona data center was online on November 14, 2014. Its discussion of a nearby 140 MW wind project describes grid-side generation and must not be treated as facility capacity, facility load, or annual electricity use.

sources.title: Meta Announces New Expansion to Altoona Campus, New Hardhat in Hand Graduates
sources.notes: Seventh-expansion announcement reports more than $2.5 billion of campus investment, more than 400 people working in operations each day, more than $2.6 million in community grants and sponsorships, and a planned greater-than-five-million-square-foot campus at completion. It projects an average 1,000 construction workers over a twelve-year 2013-2025 build period, names Turner Construction as general contractor, and describes seven graduates of an eight-week training class, but gives no worker residence, wages, placements, supplier payments, or selected-building allocation.

sources.title: 2025 Environmental Data Index
sources.notes: Facility tables report Altoona electricity consumption of 980,000, 950,705, 1,043,606, 1,243,306, and 1,585,392 MWh for 2020-2024 and water withdrawal of 151, 140, 199, 173, and 242 megaliters for those years. Electricity is normalized to kWh in records. The water series is retained in the search trail because the governed evidence dictionary has no actual facility-water metric; it is not coerced into the planned-water metric. Meta's separate companywide construction-water total cannot be allocated to Altoona.

sources.title: Iowa Economic Development Authority Annual Report FY2025
sources.notes: High Quality Jobs program tables list Siculus contracts 13-HQJTC-040 and 19-HQJPTC-025. The first reports $699.5 million contracted capital investment, a $26 million maximum tax benefit, 41 reported jobs, and $4,372,163,473 total project cost at completion; the second reports $400 million contracted capital investment, zero maximum tax benefit, 31 reported jobs, and $817.9 million total project cost at completion. The report does not establish whether spending or employees overlap across awards, whether the maximum benefit was claimed, or how either award maps to the selected building.

sources.title: Iowa Data Center Tax Incentives
sources.notes: Historical program table lists the original 2013 Siculus award at $299.5 million capital investment, an $18 million maximum tax benefit, 31 jobs, and a 2019 completion target. Later IEDA reports show amended values and dates, so this source is retained as contract-history evidence and its superseded projections are not duplicated as current records.

sources.title: Facebook, Inc. 2017 Form 10-K Exhibit 21.1, List of Subsidiaries
sources.notes: The filed subsidiary list identifies Siculus, Inc. as a Facebook subsidiary. This supports continuity between Siculus state, city, tax, and environmental records and the Facebook/Meta operator identity; it does not allocate assets or payments to Altoona buildings.

sources.title: Final Title V Operating Permit 18-TV-007R1, Siculus Inc.
sources.notes: Final permit for Siculus at 100 Share Way, facility ID 92-6988, effective April 8, 2024 through April 7, 2029. The insignificant-activities inventory lists 84 CAT 3.0/3.1 MW engines, one 600 kW engine, two 1.0 MW CAT engines, 24 Cummins 3 MW engines, and one Cummins 1 MW engine, for 112 permitted emergency engines campus-wide; ATN and PCI group labels show the permit is broader than the selected footprint. Permitted equipment and potential emissions are not actual run hours, fuel use, emissions, or electricity capacity.

sources.title: Facility Explorer site detail for Siculus Inc.
sources.notes: State facility detail identifies operating Siculus site 310199764 at 100 Share Way and its Title V air program. A separate construction-site record, facility 312068167, identifies NPDES General Permit No. 2 program 23219-22977 beginning in 2013 and later discontinued; the linked stormwater detail did not yield quantitative discharge or cost data.

sources.title: Altoona City Council Minutes, November 18, 2024
sources.notes: Council approved a first amendment to the Siculus development agreement for temporary buildings. Minutes describe a $6-per-square-foot PILOT and estimate roughly $810,000 per year while the temporary buildings are used; this is a prospective gross municipal-revenue estimate, not a bill, receipt, selected-building payment, or net fiscal result.

sources.title: Altoona City Council Minutes, March 15, 2021

project_updates.title: Boundary and chronology audit — selected building remains distinct from campus
project_updates.notes: The inventory target is one 315,400-square-foot building footprint named Facebook Altoona Data Center 1, while operator, IEDA, city, tax and DNR sources overwhelmingly describe the multi-building Siculus/Meta Altoona campus. Facebook announced the project April 23, 2013 and reported the Altoona data center online November 14, 2014. No public IM3-to-ATN building-number, street-address, parcel, incentive-award or equipment crosswalk was found, so every campus and company-county observation remains unallocated. Siculus is a Facebook subsidiary and Facebook's corporate rename to Meta is operator continuity, not a predecessor transfer.
project_updates.project_description: Meta's Altoona project is an operating multi-building data-center campus in Altoona, Polk County, Iowa, held in public records through its Siculus subsidiary. Facebook announced the project in April 2013 and reported the data center online on November 14, 2014; subsequent expansions extended construction into the 2020s. This account follows the selected 315,400-square-foot IM3 building footprint while keeping campus-wide investment, employment, utility, permit, incentive, and community figures unallocated from that building.

project_updates.title: State incentive and compliance audit — two awards retained without summation
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: IEDA FY2025 annual report, earlier IEDA data-center incentive table, indexed IEDA county reports, Siculus contract numbers 13-HQJTC-040 and 19-HQJPTC-025, award/completion dates, contracted capital investment, maximum tax benefit, reported jobs and total project cost at completion. Direct records preserve each current contract's expected and actual amounts and reported jobs. Contract 13's maximum benefit is a ceiling, not realized credits; contract 19 reports zero maximum benefit. The historical $18 million/$299.5 million version of contract 13 is superseded by the current $26 million/$699.5 million table. No claims-paid, credits-certified, sales/use-tax refund, benefit-disbursement, wage-compliance detail, building allocation, or award-overlap reconciliation was found.

project_updates.title: Assessor and tax audit — multi-parcel search did not yield a selected-building tax account
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: Polk County Treasurer and assessor-linked interactive property-tax search by Siculus company name, 100 Share Way address and sample parcel details. The company query returned 34 rows including duplicates/inactive accounts and parcels such as 292310300006, 792303400002, 792303400006, 792310100001, 792310200001/006/007/008, 792310300001/006 and 792310401002-005; the DNR address query returned no exact row. Sampled accounts 292310300006 and 792310200002 were inactive and had no bill. Because the active parcel set, real/personal property accounts, abatements, PILOT accounts and selected building are not reconciled, no assessed value, tax bill, payment, tax distribution or tax-derived fiscal model is retained; missing evidence is not recorded as zero.

project_updates.title: Permit and planning audit — later phase components retained at permit scope
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: Altoona City Council minutes and City-issued building-permit reports republished by local economic development for 2016-2020, using Siculus, Facebook, Meta, Share Way, ATN, foundation, balance of construction, fence and guard-house queries. Quantified records were found for 300 Share Way foundation work, ATN 5/6 foundation/paving and balance work, campus fencing, and two guard houses. These later phase and campus-component permit values are preserved separately as issued values, not actual costs, and not summed into state investment. No original-building permit number, certificate of occupancy, final valuation, contractor payment, or IM3-to-ATN crosswalk was found.

project_updates.title: Utility and infrastructure audit — agreements and a commitment found, bills absent
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: Altoona council minutes, water and sewer code/rate materials, infrastructure and will-serve agreement indexes, City development-agreement reporting, MidAmerican/grid reporting, and queries for Siculus/Meta meter, demand, electricity, water, sewer, franchise fee, pump station and reimbursement. City minutes confirm infrastructure and will-serve amendments but disclose no flows, rates, invoices or payments. Reporting identifies a $500,000 company pump-station commitment, retained only as a source projection. Meta's facility table supplies electricity consumption directly. No utility bill, electricity demand, rate, payment, wastewater flow, water-meter series, completed infrastructure contribution, municipal service cost, or selected-building share was found.

project_updates.title: Environmental audit — permitted equipment and resource observations kept distinct
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: Iowa DNR Facility Explorer operating site 310199764, construction site 312068167, Title V permit 18-TV-007R1, NPDES General Permit No. 2 index, Polk County air-source listings, Meta environmental data, and exact facility/address/entity queries. The final air permit supports 112 permitted emergency engines across ATN and PCI groups; no engine is allocated to the selected building and permit limits are not actual emissions or generation. Meta reports annual Altoona electricity and water withdrawals for 2020-2024. Electricity is normalized directly; water values of 151, 140, 199, 173 and 242 megaliters remain documented here because the governed dictionary lacks an actual-water metric. No site-specific discharge, fuel-use, actual-emissions, generator-run-hour, water-payment, wastewater-payment, or construction-water allocation was found.

project_updates.title: Workforce, procurement and supplier audit — identities found, spending absent
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: Meta expansion releases, Turner Construction/project references, Hardhat in Hand and DMACC training references, Iowa Workforce Development WARN notices, contractor/trade coverage, and queries combining Siculus/Meta/Altoona with contractor, subcontractor, vendor, supplier, procurement, payroll, wage, apprentice, local hire and resident. Meta names Turner as general contractor and reports a seven-person training cohort; the 2025 WARN table identifies an IES Communications layoff at 500 Share Way. These establish supplier/workforce activity but no invoices, contract values, annual supplier spend, establishment geography, locally retained share, payroll, benefits, job placements, worker residence, occupation mix, or selected-building allocation. Supplier contribution therefore remains an explicit gap and no multiplier is applied.

project_updates.title: Community and recipient audit — direct funding retained with overlap controls
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: Meta Altoona grants/sponsorship statements and Community Action Grant recipient pages, Altoona local archives, Iowa State University Extension Polk County, schools and nonprofits, using grant, donation, sponsorship, recipient and amount queries. The operator reports more than $2.6 million cumulatively through December 2021; a local 2015 announcement identifies $103,000 to 25 nonprofits and schools, and ISU Extension independently confirms a Meta-supported STEM event but gives no amount. The 2015 amount is nested within the cumulative total and must not be summed. No complete annual ledger, recipient-level reconciliation, in-kind valuation, volunteer-hour value, or causal outcome measurement was found.

project_updates.title: Expansion, adjacent project and continuity audit — phases kept separate
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: operator announcements from 2013-2026, local permit reports, DNR ATN/PCI equipment labels, Siculus corporate identity, and reporting for adjacent Polk County data-center construction. Operator sources describe at least seven expansions and a campus expected to exceed five million square feet; permit records specifically identify later ATN 5/6 work. No evidence supports treating all later buildings, adjacent confidential projects, regional wind generation, or every Siculus parcel as the selected original building. Corporate sources support Facebook-to-Meta/Siculus continuity, so no predecessor asset transfer or pre-acquisition baseline is inferred.

project_updates.title: Fiscal and public-cost audit — projections found, realized ledger absent
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: 2019 and 2024 development-agreement reporting, council minutes, IEDA benefit tables, Polk tax accounts, City budgets/minutes and searches for PILOT, franchise fee, property tax, abatement, refund, incentive, tax credit, public service, fire, police, road, water, sewer and infrastructure cost. The 2024 minutes support an approximately $810,000 annual PILOT projection for temporary buildings, and IEDA reports a $26 million maximum benefit for contract 13. Neither is a realized payment. No same-scope series for PILOT receipts, property taxes paid, credits claimed/certified, abatements in dollars, franchise-fee retention, recurring service costs, public infrastructure funding or net municipal/county fiscal result was found.

project_updates.title: County-statistics audit — governed Polk County panel reviewed as context
project_updates.notes: Sources checked: governed Polk County FIPS 19153 panel for 2001-2024, BEA regional GDP/personal-income tables, BLS QCEW county employment and wage files, industry classifications, nearby Iowa counties, and the candidate chronology. Polk County already hosted Microsoft's first West Des Moines data center by 2012, Meta construction began in 2013, the first Meta center was online in 2014, and multi-building construction continued through later expansions. County outcomes are descriptive context only because there is no single campus treatment date, selected-building exposure measure, source-registered comparison group, or isolation from concurrent hyperscale, population, and metro development.

project_updates.title: County outcome model decisions — employment, wages and GDP rejected separately
project_updates.notes: Employment candidates: simple Polk County before/after change — REJECTED because total employment combines all industries and overlapping 2013 construction, 2014 operation and later phases; matched-county or synthetic comparison — REJECTED because no pre-registered untreated donor pool with comparable metro growth, industry mix and pre-trends was found; multiplier scaling from 31, 41, 400 or 1,300 workers — REJECTED because definitions overlap and payroll, residence, local purchases and applicable coefficients are absent. Wage candidates: QCEW before/after or matched-county gap — REJECTED because county average wages are composition-sensitive and treatment/donor validity fails; imputed project payroll — REJECTED because headcounts are not FTE and occupation, wage, benefit and residence inputs are missing. GDP candidates: before/after or matched comparison — REJECTED for the same timing, donor and concurrent-investment failures; input-output scaling — REJECTED because cumulative campus investment and permit values are not dated local final demand and local-purchase shares/coefficients are absent. All three governed county comparison metrics remain missing individually.

project_updates.title: Last-resort contribution-model gate — zero eligible estimates
project_updates.notes: Candidate-by-candidate result after direct-source gap closure: selected-building investment, construction, jobs, electricity or water by floor-area allocation — REJECTED because no IM3-to-ATN crosswalk exists, infrastructure/equipment intensity is nonuniform, and the greater-than-five-million-square-foot denominator is a future campus projection; construction job-years/payroll from 1,300 peak or 1,000 average workers — REJECTED because neither supplies hours, duration by phase, wages, benefits or residence; indirect/induced effects from state costs, cumulative investment or permits — REJECTED because bases overlap, permit value is not expenditure, annual timing and local purchase shares are absent, and no applicable source-registered multipliers were found; operations payroll/multipliers — REJECTED because 31/41 program jobs and 400-plus daily on-site people have different unknown definitions and no payroll; property tax/PILOT/net fiscal estimates — REJECTED because parcel, rate, abatement, bill, receipt, benefit realization and service-cost inputs do not reconcile; utility payments or capacity-factor estimates — REJECTED because rates, demand, meters and bills are absent and wind nameplate MW is not facility load; annual water in gallons — REJECTED as unnecessary unit conversion without a governed actual-water metric, while facility withdrawal is fully documented in source units; community annualization/multipliers — REJECTED because cumulative and 2015 amounts overlap and outcomes are not monetized. Zero modeled records are justified.

project_updates.title: Contribution-account disposition — candidate pending adversarial review
project_updates.notes: Direct observations now cover investment, construction, operations, fiscal, public costs, resources and community; suppliers remain unsupported. The project fragment adds 27 records: 20 reported actuals and seven source projections. Together with the one existing baseline construction-peak record, the project has 28 direct records, 21 reported actuals, seven projections and zero modeled estimates. Material gaps remain for selected-building allocation, supplier/local spending, construction and operating payroll, realized incentives, actual tax/PILOT receipts, public-service costs, utility payments, annual water normalization under the current metric dictionary, and all three causal county outcomes. This initial provisional handoff is candidate_pending_adversarial_review and is not accepted evidence.
